question: Does a change in HPC-exit total pressure (P30) have a defensible causal effect on HPC-exit temperature (T30) during the documented FD001 HPC degradation scenario?
selection_reason: Both measurements are documented FD001 readings associated with the HPC component. They are used to test the integration contract, not to assert that one physically causes the other.

evidence.supports: FD001 contains one documented HPC degradation fault mode.

evidence.source_title: Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation
evidence.supports: P30 and T30 are documented C-MAPSS measurements.

assumptions: The metadata in fd001_sensors.py accurately represents the cited NASA sensor definitions.
The source and target roles are prototype inputs and do not establish a causal direction.
limitations: No causal discovery or causal inference method has been executed.
Sensor measurements are observations, not physical interventions.
The temporal and multi engine structure of FD001 is not modeled here.
This inquiry cannot support a maintenance recommendation.
